quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Protecting yourself by passing bad drivers in traffic.
Staying very close behind the car in front of you.
Quickly switching lanes to avoid traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you notice dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you stay safe around reckless, careless, or intoxicated drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: You notice a problem with your vehicle that could affect safety. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have enough money.
Drive slowly.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any problem that affects safe driving must be fixed right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: A train is coming and it is close or moving fast. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Do not cross until the train has fully passed.
Cross at your own risk.
Find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross until the train has fully passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is coming and could be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or they are broken.

questions.question: A car is tailgating you on a multilane highway. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to match their speed.
Move to another lane and let them pass.
Slow down but stay in your lane.
Let them pass, then tailgate them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If someone is following too closely, move to the right lane to let them pass. Use the left lane only to pass slower traffic.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of an oncoming train.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After stopping completely and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After stopping completely and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the light or being careless.

questions.question: How can you help avoid rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Let your car slow before pressing the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas to let your car slow, then apply steady brake pressure. Your brake lights will warn other drivers.

questions.question: You want to change from the right lane to the left lane on a highway. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in your blind spot. Always signal before you move.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving.
Driving too fast for conditions.
Following other cars too closely.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal to show other drivers your plan.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers your plan. Look for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Drives slowly all the time.
Watches what other drivers do.
Drives at the same speed always.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Even good drivers get distracted. A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: When should drivers use one-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing up or using vehicle controls like signals, radio, or wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When backing up or using vehicle controls like signals, radio, or wipers.
questions.explanation: Use one hand to steer only when backing up or operating vehicle controls that require you to reach away from the steering wheel.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the side of the road with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop while the red lights flash or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: You can prevent alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding before drinking that you will not drive.
Saying no if someone offers you a drink while you are driving.
Calling a taxi.
Doing any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doing any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol changes your judgment, making it hard to make safe choices after you have started drinking.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less strong with beer than with wine.
Is less strong with wine than with beer.
Is strongest with hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type does not matter—only how much alcohol enters your bloodstream.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Turn and look through the rear window over your shoulder.
Only use a backup camera.
Stick your head out the driver's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn and look through the rear window over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When backing up, turn your head and look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or a backup camera.

questions.question: How can you prevent highway hypnosis?

options.text: Start your drive well-rested.
Stop regularly, even if you do not feel tired.
Keep your eyes moving around.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Long drives can make you feel bored and drowsy, called highway hypnosis. To avoid this, start your trip well-rested. Stop often, even if you do not feel tired. Move your eyes around the road to avoid eye strain from looking in one spot.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means do not make a U-turn. Do not turn around where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Drivers should use hand-over-hand steering:

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing up or using vehicle controls like signals, radio, or wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning the wheel at low speeds.
questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering to turn at low speeds, like at an intersection or when parking. Place your left hand at 8 or 9 o'clock and your right hand at 3 or 4 o'clock on the wheel.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Opposing traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of opposing traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always keep children properly fastened into a seat.

questions.question: When should you use your parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park.
Only when you park on a hill.
Only when you park on a busy street.
Only when you park in a parking lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park.
questions.explanation: Use your parking brake every time you park, whether your car is manual or automatic and whether the ground is flat or hilly.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: If you stop along the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. Make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow down and change lanes to give it extra space. If changing lanes is not safe, slow below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light.
A flashing red light.
A solid yellow light.
A solid red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you must slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic signal means a ____ light will soon appear.

options.text: Flashing yellow.
Steady green.
Steady red.
Flashing red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear soon.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: The driver plans to turn left.
The driver plans to turn right.
The driver plans to stop.
The driver plans to start moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver plans to stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they intend to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times a minute to watch for tailgaters or cars approaching too fast. If someone is following you too closely, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end collisions happen when cars follow too closely.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, give the right-of-way to other drivers, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you are driving through an intersection
When you are passing a bicyclist
When you see a child about to run into the street
When you are parallel parking

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: What is a hazard when driving in autumn?

options.text: Wet leaves on the road
Rain and mist on the road
Less daylight hours
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Wet leaves make roads slippery and dangerous. Reduced daylight from the end of daylight saving time causes poor visibility. Rain and mist mix with oil and grease on the road, making it slick. Slow down and increase your distance from the car ahead of you in these conditions.

questions.question: What must a driver do around pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation. It is your responsibility to watch for pedestrians and yield to them, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop
No U-turn
Yield
Do not enter

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign
Stop sign
Hospital sign
Railroad warning sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn
Curve ahead
Turn right or left
Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow
questions.explanation: This one-way sign tells you that traffic moves only in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: How should you adjust your seat belt?

options.text: Loosely
Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen
Hidden under the seat
To stop the seat belt warning light

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with enough room to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Maintain a safe distance from the car ahead
Decrease your distance from the car ahead
Stop completely before changing lanes
Swerve in and out of traffic as fast as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a safe distance from the car ahead
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance from the car in front when changing lanes. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure no vehicles are in your path or entering your lane.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Proceed slowly through the intersection
Stop, then proceed when the way is clear
Stop, then proceed when the light turns green or green arrow appears
You may turn in the direction the arrow points

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when the light turns green or green arrow appears
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.
